maria (PM): Heads-up — large customer asked for ~20% p50 latency improvement on hosted chat API. They're also explicitly cost-sensitive. How do we prioritize latency vs throughput vs unit cost here?

devin (Eng): For model-family A: 20% p50 reduction needs smaller batching and more aggressive kernel paths. That usually cuts throughput ~25–35% unless we add capacity. Unit cost goes up ~20–30% for same QPS.

lena (Data): For their workload (short sessions, avg 120 tokens) batching wins are minimal. Latency-first makes sense for this profile.

alex (Design): From product UX: is this a global platform mode (latency-priority) or a per-customer setting? Rollout/communication differ a lot.

san (SRE): We can implement a "low-latency" runtime profile: smaller max batch, tighter batch timeout, reserved slots. Ops complexity + scheduler fragmentation will increase.

maria (PM): Proposal: run a quick prioritization using a compact scorecard (adapted RICE): Reach = #requests affected, Impact = user-facing error/latency improvement, Confidence, Effort. Also add an explicit Cost-Delta metric so sales can see $ impact.

devin (Eng): Quick back-of-envelope: Reach ~400k qpm, Impact 7/10, Confidence 0.6, Effort ~4w eng + infra config, cost delta ~$6k/mo at current util.

lena (Data): +1 on cost-delta column. Also we should track completion-quality drift (same prompts -> similar outputs) as a launch gating metric.

alex (Design): Suggested launch criteria: 1) targeted p50 met on canary, 2) <5% token-cost increase for avg workload, 3) no regression in completion quality metrics, 4) observability dashboards live.

maria (PM): Scope options to consider: A) Light: platform toggle for hosted only (fast, low-risk). B) Mid: dedicated pools for specific enterprise customers (more capex/ops). C) Deep: runtime kernel / quant path changes for global improvement (high effort, long term).

san (SRE): Recommended sequence: A -> B for priority customers -> C if we need persistent global gains. Canary to 5% traffic, escalate to 25% if stable. Add auto-rollback on p95 or error-rate regressions.

devin (Eng): For canary we'd like these telemetry hooks: `kvcache_hit_rate`, `batch_size_distribution`, `tokens_per_second`, `cost_per_1M_tokens`. Also a simple script to flip profile per-route. Example canary guard:

```
if p95_latency_canary > baseline_p95 * 1.05 or cost_delta > 1.05:
  rollback()
else:
  continue_rollout()
```

maria (PM): Perfect. I'll author a short PRD with the adapted RICE table and three scope options + canary plan. Will ask Sales to rank customer asks by willingness-to-pay (helps decide B vs A).

alex (Design): UX note: when customers toggle latency mode, we should show expected cost change in the Console before they confirm.

lena (Data): I'll prepare perf test dataset mirroring the customer's short-chat distribution so we can validate quality + perf at scale.

ci-bot: perf-canary-job queued -> staging.

maria (PM): Thanks all — syncing tomorrow 11:00 to finalize numbers and owners. If anyone has data to add to the RICE-ish table before then, drop it here or ping @maria. :thumbsup:
